data_disclaimer: All parameter values are synthetic round numbers chosen to exercise the importer; none are vendor, paper or measured data.

conventions.formulas: exact strings stored in the file; openpyxl writes no cached values, so a reader must evaluate them (post-2007 functions carry the _xlfn. prefix, which SheetJS strips by default)
conventions.expected_values: one number per formula cell, computed in Python with IEEE-754 doubles following the formula's own operation order; compare with the per-workbook tolerance (rel OR abs)
conventions.expected_methods: list of {tag, cells, optional_cells?, note?}; a cell may carry several tags (e.g. switchover_weighted and parallel_product_complement on the same cell). Tests should assert cells ⊆ detected ⊆ cells ∪ optional_cells per tag
conventions.untagged_formula_cells: formula cells that match no catalogue tag (complements, pass-throughs, differences, 1/MTBF); listed so a fingerprinter can be checked for false positives
conventions.columns: role -> column letter; base roles: name, level, count, mtbf_h, mttr_h, fit, lambda_per_h, availability, unavailability, redundancy, switchover_success, auto_fraction, mttr_auto_h, mttr_manual_h, mttr_effective_h, notes; extension roles used here: unit_availability (F2, F3), afr_pct_per_year and availability_pct (F9)

tree_node.name: trimmed display name
tree_node.count: number of identical copies of the node in series that the engine must apply (A_node = A^count); 1 when the sheet does not apply the quantity
tree_node.qty_cell: raw value of the quantity column (informational; equals n on homogeneous redundancy rows, may be ignored by the sheet as in F4)
tree_node.k, n: voting parameters; parallel means k = 1; null for leaf and series
tree_node.homogeneous: true when the row describes n identical units whose parameters are in params and children is empty
tree_node.params: input values exactly as stored (numbers; redundancy text)
tree_node.derived: values of formula cells belonging to the row (λ from FIT, MTTR_eff, μ, MTBF from AFR)
tree_node.cells: role -> cell address for every parameter and result cell (provenance)
tree_node.alt_cells: other cells computing the same node's availability with another method

evaluation.leaf: A_unit = mtbf/(mtbf+mttr), or 1/(1+λ·mttr) when λ is given, or the percent/100; A = A_unit^count
evaluation.parallel: homogeneous: 1-(1-A_unit)^n, with switchover success c: c·(1-(1-A_unit)^n) + (1-c)·A_unit; heterogeneous (F6/F7): 1-Π(1-A_child)
evaluation.ctmc (F5): 3-state chain with one repair crew; availability = π(2 up)+π(1 up)

workbooks.title: Series system, English headers, per-unit availability raised to the quantity

expected_methods.note: per-unit A = C/(C+D) raised to Qty: (C/(C+D))^B; the exponent is the series multiplicity

untagged_formula_cells.why: complement U = 1 - A; no catalogue tag

ambiguities: Qty is applied as an exponent inside the Availability formula ((C/(C+D))^B), so the leaf parameters are per unit and count = Qty.
Two system rows: row 8 (exact PRODUCT) and row 9 (1 - SUM(U) rare-event approximation) describe the same system; the tree root is row 8 and row 9 is an alternative-method cell.

workbooks.title: FIT to lambda, 1+1 redundancy with switchover success, Chinese headers

expected_methods.note: λ = FIT * 1E-9
sub-expression 1-(1-F)^2 inside the switchover weighting; the exponent 2 gives n
H*(A_parallel) + (1-H)*(A_unit) with H = 倒换成功率

untagged_formula_cells.why: no redundancy (冗余方式 = 无): the group availability is a pass-through of the unit availability

ambiguities: 数量 = 2 on a 1+1 row counts the two units of the pair (n = 2), not two groups in series; the exponent 2 in the group formula confirms it. The tree therefore has count = 1, n = 2 for those rows.
倒换成功率 is blank on the row without redundancy.
Two availability-like columns: F (单机可用度, per unit) and I (组可用度, what the parent consumes). The tree's availability cell is column I.

workbooks.title: 2-of-3 and 3-of-4 groups in explicit-sum, COMBIN and BINOM.DIST form

expected_methods.note: A^n + n*A^(n-1)*(1-A): the terms i = n and i = n-1 of the k-of-n sum
1-BINOM.DIST(k-1, n, A, TRUE) = P(at least k of n up); stored as _xlfn.BINOM.DIST

untagged_formula_cells.why: 1/1 row: group availability is a pass-through of the unit availability

ambiguities: Columns G, H and I compute the same group availability three ways (they agree to ~1e-16); the tree's availability cell is G, H and I are listed under availability_alt. An importer should pick one and report the others as cross-checks, not create three groups.
Qty (n) holds the number of units in the voting group; k and n also appear as text 'k/n' in column F. count = 1 in the tree.
BINOM.DIST is stored as _xlfn.BINOM.DIST in the file (required for post-2007 functions); SheetJS strips the prefix by default.
Three system cells (G5, H5, I5) are all PRODUCT of their own column.

workbooks.title: Effective MTTR as a mixture of automatic and manual recovery

expected_methods.note: D*E + (1-D)*F with D = 自动恢复比例
1/(1+λ·MTTR_eff) using the mixture MTTR

ambiguities: Qty (column B) is not referenced by any formula: the λ column is the aggregate failure rate of the whole row (see the 备注 column), so the tree uses count = 1 and lambda_scope = row_aggregate. Contrast F1, where Qty is an exponent.
Mixed zh/en headers on one row.

workbooks.title: 1+1 hot standby solved as a 3-state Markov chain with MMULT/MINVERSE/TRANSPOSE

evaluation.repair_policy: single repair crew: '0 up' -> '1 up' at μ (not 2μ); this is why B22 differs from the independent-units value B27 by B28
evaluation.closed_form: π(2 up) = 1/(1+2ρ+2ρ²), π(1 up) = 2ρ·π(2 up), π(0 up) = 2ρ²·π(2 up), ρ = λ/μ

expected_methods.note: INDEX(MMULT(MINVERSE(M), b), r, 1) per cell, no CSE arrays; M is built in B13:D15 with INDEX(TRANSPOSE(Q), r, c) and a row of ones, b in F13:F15
EXP(-λt)*(1+λt): cold-standby mission reliability without repair; a different 口径 (reliability over t, not availability) and NOT part of the tree

untagged_formula_cells.pattern: generator matrix entries from λ and μ

untagged_formula_cells.why: rate from MTTR; no catalogue tag
Σπ check, availability = π(2 up)+π(1 up), unavailability = π(0 up), Δ vs independent units

tolerance.note: π(0 up) ≈ 1.28e-8 is obtained from an O(1) matrix solve, so Excel and any other solver agree with it only to ~1e-16 absolute (~1e-8 relative); compare the small cells (B20, B23, B28) absolutely

ambiguities: Block layout, no header row and no component table: the model is a single 1+1 group whose parameters are label/value pairs (A3:B5).

Availability is the sum of two state probabilities (B22 = B18+B19), not a formula over component availabilities; the importer should recognise the MMULT/MINVERSE block and treat the chain as one node solved by CTMC.

The chain uses one repair crew (0 up -> 1 up at μ). An engine that models the pair as two independent repairable units (2μ) reproduces B27, not B22; the difference B28 = B27 - B22 ≈ +6.4e-9 (independent units are more available than the single-crew chain) is intended.
B31 is a mission-reliability formula (EXP) sitting on the same sheet; it must be tagged standby_exp but kept out of the availability tree.

workbooks.title: Tree given by a 层级 (level) column, Chinese headers

expected_methods.note: rows 6-9 use (D/(D+E))^C (Qty as exponent), rows 11, 12, 14, 15 use D/(D+E)
F3 = PRODUCT(F4,F10,F13) non-contiguous list; F4 = F5*F9 chained; F5 = PRODUCT(F6:F8) range
F10 = 1-(1-F11)*(1-F12); F13 = 1-PRODUCT(G14:G15) over the 不可用度 column

untagged_formula_cells.why: complement U = 1 - A; no catalogue tag (but F6/F7 parallel 2N formulas reference these cells)

ambiguities: Row 1 is a merged title (A1:I1); the header is row 2.
The root row has 层级 = 0, which is not a dotted prefix of '1', '2', '3': rows whose level has no dot are children of the single level-0 row. The formula F3 = PRODUCT(F4,F10,F13) confirms it.

Level cells are mixed types: 0, 1, 2, 3 are stored as numbers, dotted levels ('1.1', '1.1.1') as text. Real sheets also store 1.1 as the number 1.1 (and then '1.10' collides with '1.1'); the fixture avoids that collision but an importer must coerce numeric levels to strings.
F13 (供电子系统 2N) references the 不可用度 column G14:G15 rather than the 可用度 column, so the formula graph must map G -> 1-F to identify the children rows 14 and 15.
Mixed depth: 1.2 管理节点 is a leaf directly under 计算子系统 while 1.1 计算机柜 is a group.
Redundancy text '2N' and '1+1 (双平面)' both mean k=1 of n=2.

workbooks.title: Same tree as F6, hierarchy given by leading spaces in the name and row outline levels

indent.unit: 2 leading spaces per depth level in the Component cell

expected_methods.note: rows 5-8 use (C/(C+D))^B (Qty as exponent), rows 10, 11, 13, 14 use C/(C+D)
E2 = PRODUCT(E3,E9,E12) non-contiguous list; E3 = E4*E8 chained; E4 = PRODUCT(E5:E7) range
E9 = 1-(1-E10)*(1-E11); E12 = 1-PRODUCT(F13:F14) over the Unavailability column

untagged_formula_cells.why: complement U = 1 - A; no catalogue tag (but F6/F7 parallel 2N formulas reference these cells)

ambiguities: No level column: depth = (leading spaces in Component) / 2 = Excel row outline level. Both cues agree; the root row has no outline level (0).

Excel's default outline convention is 'summary row below detail'; this sheet sets summaryBelow = false because parents sit above their children. SheetJS exposes row levels via ws['!rows'][i].level; check whether it exposes outlinePr before relying on it.
Leading spaces are stored in the shared string (xml:space='preserve'); the manifest's node.name is trimmed, node.name_cell_raw keeps the spaces.
E12 (Power subsystem 2N) references the Unavailability column F13:F14; map F -> 1-E to find the children.

workbooks.title: Series system whose headline uses 1 - sum(U) while an adjacent cell uses PRODUCT(A)

expected_methods.note: U = λ·MTTR first-order approximation (λ·MTTR is 0.018-0.04 here, so it is visibly off)
the sheet's headline number

untagged_formula_cells.why: λ = 1/MTBF; no tag in the catalogue (closest: fit_to_lambda / afr_to_mtbf are other conversions)
ΣU helper next to the 1-ΣU cell

ambiguities: The sheet's headline 'System availability' (G8) is the rare-event approximation 1-ΣU built on first-order U = λ·MTTR; the exact PRODUCT sits one row below (G9). The tree root is G9; G8 is recorded under alt_cells and the reconciliation table must show the difference (G10).
Two stacked approximations: U = λ·MTTR per row (instead of MTTR/(MTBF+MTTR)) and 1-ΣU for the series.
MTBF values (2000-6000 h) are deliberately low so the approximations are visibly wrong (≥ 1e-3).

workbooks.title: Availability entered in percent, AFR in %/year

expected_methods.note: MTBF = 8760/(AFR/100) with AFR in %/year
A = F/100 for percent entered as a number
(D/(D+E))^B with Qty as exponent

untagged_formula_cells.why: fraction -> percent for display; the inverse of percent_to_fraction, no catalogue tag
F5 stores 0.9999 with number format 0.00% (displays 99.99%), so no /100 is applied

ambiguities: Column F (可用度(%)) mixes inputs and formulas: 99.95 and 99.9 are plain numbers (format 0.00) that the sheet divides by 100; 0.9999 in F5 has the percent number format and is used without /100; F2, F6, F7 are formulas (=G*100) for display.
The percent/fraction decision must come from the formula (or the number format), not from the '%' in the header alone.
D2 and D6 are formula cells (MTBF derived from AFR), so the leaf's mtbf_h is a computed value with provenance to the AFR cell.
The /100 inside 8760/(C/100) may or may not be reported as percent_to_fraction; D2 and D6 are listed as optional_cells for that tag.
Roles afr_pct_per_year and availability_pct are extensions beyond the base role list.
